mathematical_semantic_assessment.full_negation: Both language versions require the nuclear-norm unit ball to be a polynomial image of a spectrahedral cone. The final theorem rules out a polynomial image of any genuine nonnegative-scaling cone in every finite real dimension. This broader negative result covers the source representation clause and therefore negates the complete source conjunction, regardless of further explicitness, generalized matrix inequality, or SDP requirements. It does not assert impossibility of other SDP formulations.
mathematical_semantic_assessment.genuine_definitions: The full tensor space has all eight complex entries; factors are complex two-dimensional Euclidean spaces. Decomposition costs are sums of products of genuine factor norms over unrestricted finite lists of pure tensors. No coordinate bound or target representation is included in admissibility. The standard nuclear norm is the infimum of this nonempty, bounded-below cost set. The closed ball is its actual sublevel set.
mathematical_semantic_assessment.rank_one_and_minimum: Zero terms are proved removable with tensor sum and cost preserved. A separate attained-minimum ball uses a genuine IsLeast cost, is proved contained in the infimum ball, and contains the exact zero and basis tensors with attained costs 0 and 1. The same obstruction is proved directly for that ball, so no unproved global attainment or equality of the two balls is used.
mathematical_semantic_assessment.polynomial_fields_and_quantifiers: The map uses sixteen actual real MvPolynomial coordinates for real and imaginary parts, with all coefficients and degrees allowed. Complex-coefficient polynomials on real parameters are formally represented. The source parameter dimension, cone and map are jointly existential before exact image equality. Both containment and surjectivity are used. No real-only tensor restriction, symmetry restriction, fixed degree, injectivity, interior point, or fixed decomposition length is imposed.
mathematical_semantic_assessment.cone_matrix_bridge: IsCone explicitly supplies zero membership and all nonnegative real scalings. This is weaker than spectrahedral-cone conditions and hence a legitimate larger family for the impossibility theorem. The 4-by-4 specialization uses the genuine Matrix.PosSemidef predicate under a real linear pencil; symmetry and nonnegative quadratic forms, zero membership and scaling closure are proved rather than assumed by fiat.
mathematical_semantic_assessment.proof_checked: Euclidean coordinate bounds and the triangle inequality bound each tensor coordinate by every decomposition cost and then by the infimum. Zero and the basis tensor have norms 0 and 1. Genuine polynomial ray substitution and the standard degree criterion make a scalar polynomial bounded on a cone equal to its origin value. Applying this to the real origin-coordinate of the image contradicts exact image preimages of the two distinguished tensors. Every bridge appears in the inspected Lean proofs.
mathematical_semantic_assessment.final_compiled_statement: ¬∃ n C P, TLMC1478.IsCone C ∧ P.eval '' C = TLMC1478.nuclearBall
mathematical_semantic_assessment.source_boundary: This is a disproof of an actual cone under an actual polynomial map. A normalized slice, bounded spectrahedron, rational or projective parametrization would require a different source statement.
